formulaAmount.title: Baby Formula Amount Calculator
formulaAmount.subtitle: Calculate daily formula total, amount per feed, feeding interval and scoops from your baby's age and weight. Based on Korea's Ministry of Health i-Sarang guide, with the American Academy of Pediatrics figures for comparison.

input.title: Baby details
input.monthHint: Pick completed months. Newborn means up to 4 weeks old.
input.birthHint: Enter a date to pick the age in completed months as of today. The birth date is not added to the link.
input.birthOver: Past 12 months, so the 12-month figures are shown.
input.birthErr: Enter today or an earlier date.
input.weightHint: Enter the latest weight to 0.1 kg.
input.weightErr: Enter a weight between {min} and {max} kg.
input.timesHint: Default for this age {n} · i-Sarang table {lo}–{hi}
input.timesHintSolids: Default with formula only {n} · i-Sarang table with solids {lo}–{hi}
input.breastHint: Leave at 0 if your baby only has formula.
input.scoopHint: Enter the 'water per scoop' printed on the tin or scoop. It differs by product, so always check the tin.
input.scoopErr: Enter a whole number between {min} and {max} mL.

result.label: Daily formula total
result.labelFor: Daily formula for a {w} kg baby ({age})
result.basis: {w} kg × {k} mL per kg per day (i-Sarang, rounded to 10 mL)
result.intervalSub: 24 hours divided by feeds per day
result.over: By weight the daily total would exceed {cap} mL, so it is capped at {cap} mL. Both i-Sarang and the AAP advise not going over {cap} mL a day. If your baby keeps wanting more, talk to a pediatrician.
result.feedAboveRow: The per-feed amount is above the i-Sarang table for this age ({lo}–{hi} mL). Try more feeds with less each time.
result.firstWeek: The AAP advises starting with no more than 30–60 mL per feed in the first week.
result.solids: Once solids start around 6 months, formula intake drops. The daily total above is for formula only; with solids, see the daily amount in the age table below.
result.aap: By the AAP rule (about 166 mL per kg a day, up to 960 mL) it is about {daily} mL a day · about {feed} mL per feed.
result.aapOlder: The AAP describes about 180–240 mL per feed, 4–5 times a day, around 6 months.

mixed.title: Formula for mixed feeding (estimate)
mixed.note: Breast milk intake can't be measured, so this assumes each breastfeed equals one formula feed. Watch weight gain and wet diapers too.
mixed.allBreast: All feeds are breastfeeds, so no formula amount is calculated.

care.title: These are averages
care.body: The results are averages. Watch your baby's hunger and fullness cues, weight gain and wet diapers, and talk to a pediatrician if you are worried, for example if your baby feeds poorly or isn't gaining weight.

table.title: Formula feeding by age (i-Sarang table)
table.note: The formula feeding table from i-Sarang, the Ministry of Health and Welfare's parenting portal. Daily amounts from 5 months assume the baby also eats solids.

basis.title: How it is calculated
items: Daily total = weight × formula per kg per day. i-Sarang gives 150–180 mL until 3 months, about 120 mL at 3–6 months and about 90–100 mL at 6–12 months.
i-Sarang adds that some babies, especially premature ones, may need up to 200 mL per kg.
Even if the baby wants more, don't go over 960 mL a day (i-Sarang 4–6 months, AAP 32 ounces).
Per-feed amount is the daily total divided by feeds per day. Changing the number of feeds changes the per-feed amount, not the daily total.
The AAP gives 2½ ounces (75 mL) per pound (453 g) a day, about 166 mL per kg. It is shown for comparison.

cues.title: Hunger and fullness cues
items: Hungry: puts hands to mouth, turns head toward the breast or bottle, puckers, smacks or licks lips, has clenched hands (CDC, birth to 5 months).
Full: closes mouth, turns head away from the breast or bottle, relaxes hands.
Getting fidgety or distracted during a feed may mean the baby is done. Smacking lips after emptying the bottle may mean the baby wants more (AAP).
Rather than making the baby finish a set amount, stop when the baby signals they've had enough (AAP).

prep.title: Preparing and storing formula
items: Wash your hands, clean the bottle and nipple, and make formula with boiled water cooled to at least 70°C (MFDS).
Follow the water and scoop amounts on the tin. Don't make it stronger or weaker.
Use prepared formula within 2 hours, and within 1 hour once feeding starts (CDC).
Put formula you won't use right away in the fridge immediately and use it within 24 hours (CDC).
Throw away formula left after a feed, because saliva can let bacteria grow (MFDS, CDC).
Warming in a microwave is not recommended (MSD Manual).

check.title: Checking your baby is feeding well
items: Around one week old, 6–8 wet cloth diapers (5–6 disposable) a day suggests enough feeding (i-Sarang newborn feeding).
Check steady weight gain at infant health checkups or in growth records. The child growth percentile tool shows how your baby compares.
Intake can vary from day to day (AAP). If your baby keeps feeding poorly, vomits often or has fewer wet diapers, see a pediatrician.
The AAP advises waking your baby to feed if they sleep longer than 4–5 hours in the first few weeks.

items.q: How much formula does a newborn need?
items.a: By i-Sarang, 150–180 mL per kg a day until 3 months. A 3.3 kg newborn needs about 500–590 mL a day, and the i-Sarang table lists 8–12 feeds of 50–100 mL for newborns. In the first week, start small at about 30–60 mL per feed.
At about 100 days (3 months), i-Sarang gives about 120 mL per kg a day. A 6.5 kg baby needs about 780 mL a day, or about 130 mL per feed over 6 feeds. Adjust to your baby's cues and weight gain.
Both i-Sarang and the AAP advise not going over 960 mL (about 32 ounces) a day. If your baby keeps wanting more, or takes much less, talk to a pediatrician.

items.q: How much formula with mixed feeding?
items.a: Breast milk can't be measured, so the calculator assumes each breastfeed equals one feed and splits the total by formula feeds. Adjust while watching weight gain and wet diapers.

items.q: How do I work out the number of scoops?
items.a: Divide the water per feed by the water per scoop. For example, with 20 mL per scoop, 120 mL of water takes 6 scoops. Scoop size and water amount differ by product, so always check the tin.

items.q: How does formula change after 6 months?
items.a: i-Sarang gives about 90–100 mL per kg a day at 6–12 months. With solids, the i-Sarang table drops to 700–800 mL a day at 7–8 months and 600–800 mL at 9–11 months.

items.q: How long can prepared formula be kept?
items.a: The CDC says to use it within 2 hours of preparing and within 1 hour once feeding starts, and to refrigerate formula you won't use right away and use it within 24 hours. Throw away leftovers.

sources.title: Basis and sources
sources.isarang13: Ministry of Health and Welfare i-Sarang portal, 'Feeding at 1–3 months' — 150–180 mL per kg until 3 months
sources.isarang46: i-Sarang, 'Feeding at 4–6 months' — about 120 mL per kg at 3–6 months, up to 960 mL a day, formula table
sources.isarang79: i-Sarang, 'Feeding and nutrition at 7–9 and 10–12 months' — about 90–100 mL per kg at 6–12 months
sources.isarangNewborn: i-Sarang, 'Newborn feeding' — feeds per day, judging intake by diapers
sources.aap: American Academy of Pediatrics HealthyChildren.org, 'Amount and Schedule of Baby Formula Feedings' (2022-05-16)
sources.cdcStorage: US CDC, 'Infant Formula Preparation and Storage' (2026-05-14) — 2 hours, 1 hour, 24 hours refrigerated
sources.cdcCues: US CDC, 'Signs Your Child is Hungry or Full' (2026-03-11)
sources.mfds: Korea MFDS, consumer guide to infant foods — water at 70°C or above, discard leftovers
sources.msd: MSD Manual Consumer Version, 'Formula Feeding' (reviewed 2023-09) — warming
sources.method: Daily total is weight × the i-Sarang per-kg figure, capped at 960 mL a day. mL is rounded to 10 mL and scoops to 0.5. Default feeds per age come from the i-Sarang table ranges; from 6 months the default is 5 feeds, for formula only.
sources.asOf: Checked {date}. Guidance can change, so also check at infant health checkups or appointments.
